_note: THE HOTEL ADMIN CAPABILITY CONTRACT. It was written after a bundle built with no NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE*_ADMIN flags was deployed to PRE-LIVE and served an operator surface with no Internet Packages, no Service Plans and no PMS Connection for five days: Next inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* at BUILD time, so a flag absent when `next build` runs is never substituted, the compiled comparison is permanently false in the browser, and the routes still answer by URL while the operator simply loses the navigation to them. Nothing crashes and every structural check passes. IT HAPPENED A SECOND TIME, and that is why the contract now reads as it does: a plain `next build` removed ELEVEN destinations, and the safety net did not fire because it lives at deploy time and has to be remembered. Navigation therefore no longer consults a build flag at all. edged reports which surfaces it has mounted, the sidebar offers a destination when the appliance serves it and the operator's role may read it, and a build-time variable can no longer remove anything. This file is what a build is still held to for ROUTES and NAVIGATION, and it now also forbids the flag mechanism from returning.
applies_to: PRE-LIVE appliance and every later Hotel Admin release until the contract is deliberately changed

required_build_flags._note: EMPTY BY DESIGN, AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Navigation is decided at runtime from edged's mounted surfaces, so there is no build flag whose absence can hide a destination. A flag listed here would reintroduce exactly the failure this contract exists to prevent. Packaging still supplies nothing and proves nothing about flags, because there is nothing left to prove.

required_routes._note: Operator surfaces that must exist in the built app-path route manifest. A build that cannot serve these is not a candidate for this appliance, whatever else is right about it.

required_navigation._note: THE NAVIGATION, which is the thing the operator actually sees and the thing that silently disappeared -- twice. Each entry names a destination, the route it leads to, and the edged surface that must be mounted for it to apply. Verification asserts that on an appliance serving that surface, a site_admin is offered the destination. Entries whose surface is not mounted are correctly absent: that is the appliance saying it does not run the feature, which is a different statement from a build having forgotten it.

forbidden_in_client_bundle._note: ANY capability-flag lookup in the client bundle is now a packaging failure, not just the ones that were required. Previously a residual lookup meant 'this flag went missing'; now it means 'somebody reintroduced the build-time gate', which is the mechanism that produced both outages. All five are listed so the mechanism cannot come back for one surface while the others stay correct.

minimum_rollback_contract._note: A rollback target must be able to operate this appliance. A release that predates these surfaces would remove PMS, Service Plan and Package management from the operator the moment it was served, so it is archive evidence and NOT an executable rollback, however recently it was deployed.

deliberately_absent_flags._note: STILL DARK, AND BY A STRONGER MECHANISM THAN A UI CONSTANT. These surfaces exist in the source and are not part of the authorized PRE-LIVE operator surface. What keeps them off an operator's screen is that edged DOES NOT MOUNT THEM -- the sidebar asks the appliance and is told no -- which is the same answer the build flags used to give and one that cannot be lost by forgetting a variable. The backend flags remain the authorization control and the Phase-4 DARK gate still refuses any delivered configuration that turns one on. Phase 4 is accepted at DARK maturity with NO financial traffic authorized; phases 5 and 6 are likewise not authorized here. Nothing in this delivery enables any of them.
deliberately_absent_flags.NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE4_ADMIN: not used by the product any more; Phase 4 is DARK, no financial traffic authorized
deliberately_absent_flags.NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE5_ADMIN: not used by the product any more; post-stay operator surface not authorized for PRE-LIVE
deliberately_absent_flags.NEXT_PUBLIC_PHASE6_ADMIN: not used by the product any more; guest device self-service not authorized for PRE-LIVE

authorized_consolidations._note: DESTINATIONS THAT ARE DELIBERATELY NOT TOP-LEVEL, BY PRODUCT-OWNER DECISION, AND WHICH MUST STILL BE REACHABLE. This section exists because 'not in the sidebar' and 'gone' look identical from the outside, and the difference is an authorization. An entry here is a decision on record: the destination stays built, permitted and discoverable, at a NAMED location, and the checks below hold that location the same way the sidebar contract holds the menu. Without this, a consolidation is indistinguishable from the accidental disappearance this contract was written to prevent.
authorized_consolidations.decision: Product Owner, 2026-09-21. Confirms the consolidation first made in commit cb3831ee, which until now carried only an agent's UX judgement. Both reconciliation screens are approved as NOT top-level sidebar items, and are required to be available and clearly discoverable under PMS Connection -> Advanced. Routes, permissions, the full diagnostic and evidence pages, and the direct links from PMS health when attention is needed are all to be kept. The stated goal is to avoid unnecessary sidebar clutter, NOT to hide or remove the functionality.
